guideline.text: Suspect meningitis in any child with fever and stiff neck, bulging fontanelle, convulsions, lethargy or irritability. Give the first dose of ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IM and refer urgently. Do not delay referral for tests.

message: 18 month old, fever, very irritable, stiff neck, bulging fontanelle. Boat leaves in 3 hours.
reply:
Suspect meningitis: refer on the next boat, do not wait for tests.
Give ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IM now before leaving.
Do a malaria test and treat if positive; paracetamol for fever.
Keep the child on the side, a nurse goes with the child.

guideline.text: Pale palms or conjunctiva: check for malaria, hookworm and diet. Mild or moderate anaemia: ferrous sulphate 3 mg/kg elemental iron daily for 3 months, albendazole, malaria test. Severe anaemia (very pale, breathless, heart failure) needs transfusion: refer urgently.

message: 6 year old very pale, breathless when walking, swollen feet, RDT positive. Boat tomorrow.
reply:
Severe anaemia with heart failure signs: refer on the next transport for transfusion.
Start artemether-lumefantrine by weight today for the malaria.
Keep the child resting, sitting up; small frequent meals.
Send a note: Hb not measured, very pale, breathless, oedema, RDT positive.

guideline.text: Suspect UTI in a child with fever and no other cause, pain passing urine or smelly urine. Test the urine with a dipstick. Treat with amoxicillin-clavulanate or cotrimoxazole for 7 days. Infants under 3 months and children who look very sick must be referred.

message: 4 year old girl, fever 2 days, says it hurts to wee, urine smells. Dipstick leukocytes and nitrites positive. 15 kg.
reply:
Urinary tract infection. Amoxicillin-clavulanate (or cotrimoxazole) for 7 days by weight.
Plenty of fluids, paracetamol for fever.
Review in 2 days; refer if vomiting, very unwell or no better.

guideline.text: All children with fever should have a malaria test (RDT or blood slide). Uncomplicated malaria: artemether-lumefantrine by weight twice daily for 3 days with food: 5-14 kg 1 tablet per dose, 15-24 kg 2 tablets, 25-34 kg 3 tablets. Severe malaria (unable to drink, convulsions, lethargy, severe anaemia, jaundice): give artesunate IM or rectal and refer urgently. If no test is available and fever has no other cause, treat as malaria and refer for testing.

reply:

Givim artemether-lumefantrine 1 tablet tu taem evri dei fo 3 dei wetem kaikai.
Sendem pikinini long klinik wea garem test long nekis bot fo checkim.
Lukim hem bak long 2 dei o kwiktaem sapos hem kam wos.

guideline.text: Fast breathing: 2-12 months 50 or more breaths per minute; 1-5 years 40 or more. Pneumonia (fast breathing, no chest indrawing): amoxicillin 40 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days, review in 2 days. Severe pneumonia (chest indrawing, danger signs, oxygen saturation under 90%): give the first dose of antibiotic, oxygen if available, and refer urgently.

guideline.text: Place the convulsing child on the side, protect the airway, put nothing in the mouth. If the fit lasts more than 5 minutes give rectal diazepam 0.5 mg/kg. Check blood glucose and treat hypoglycaemia. Give paracetamol for fever. Every child with a convulsion and fever needs a malaria test and must be referred to a doctor the same day.

message: Pikinini 2 yia hem fit nao, 3 minit finis, hot bodi hae. Hem stop fit nao bat hem slip tumas.
reply:
Danger sign: fit wetem hot bodi an slip tumas. Sendem nao.
Putim hem long saed, kipim airway klia, no putim eni samting long maot.
Sapos hem fit moa ova 5 minit: rectal diazepam 0.5 mg/kg.
Duim RDT, givim paracetamol, checkim sugar. Go wetem nes.
